Kento Alpha 0.9.40, build 3077

New

  • Render this in Nuke: for the nodes Kento can't render yet, Kento writes one Nuke script that pre-renders them, and puts a stand-in under each that reads the frames back. Find it in the Node Graph's toolbar (Make a Nuke Pre-render) and in File > Import and File > Export (Nuke pre-renders).

Fixes

  • The bm_CameraShake gizmo now shakes as it does in Nuke, and no longer crashes Kento. Its shake curve matches Nuke at every frame and subframe. With motion blur on, the blur itself is still a little different from Nuke's.
  • Expressions that integrate a knob over a range of frames (knob.integrate(a, b)) now work.
  • Transform's bounding box now matches Nuke's: a whole-pixel move shifts the box, and other moves grow it by the same amount Nuke does.
  • Dilate, Blur and ShuffleCopy now read past an input's bounding box as Nuke does, with the edge pixels carried on.
  • HSVTool with more than one range on (hue, saturation and brightness together) now changes the same pixels as Nuke.
  • Keymix's bounding box takes in the mask's box only when the mask is inverted, as in Nuke.
  • Inside a group, parent.width, parent.height and parent.pixel_aspect now read the group's format, so the L_Ramp and L_AspectMask gizmos look as they do in Nuke.
  • A Dissolve with more than two inputs now picks the same input as Nuke for each value of which (its third input is the mask), and saves that way too. The L_ChannelSolo gizmo now shows the right channel.

Kento Alpha 0.9.39, build 3050

New

  • ColorCorrect's test now shows the range pattern in the picture, as Nuke renders it: red and blue mark the range that weighs most (shadows black, midtones dark gray, highlights white), and green blends the ranges.
  • A camera reads ASCII FBX files (Nuke's WriteGeo writes them with its ASCII option) the same as binary ones.
  • FrameHold has Nuke's rounding mode: Whole frames (the default) holds the whole frame toward zero, so 4.6 holds frame 4; Fractional time holds the frame as set.

Fixes

  • LensDistortion2 and the Lens node on an anamorphic plate (pixels wider than tall) now distort as Nuke does. They work in the plate's pixel aspect, where before they treated its pixels as square and could be 25 pixels off at the corners.
  • Keymix now reads its inputs past their edges as Nuke does: each input's edge pixels carry on outside its box, and the mask's box joins the output's. Gizmos that key through an inverted mask, such as Spill_Correct and Match_Black_White, now match Nuke at the mask's edges.
  • An expression that reads another knob at a different frame now reads that knob's own keyframes at that frame too. The Erode_Fine gizmo, for one, now leaves the picture alone at size 0.
  • UVProject set to perspective with an Axis (not a camera) maps the texture as Nuke does.
  • Reconcile3D moves its picture as Nuke does with stabilize and an offset, and with calculate output live.
  • A Roto with nothing plugged into it gives only the channels it draws, as Nuke does.
  • Crop's presets now cut a whole number of pixels off each side, as Nuke does, instead of a fraction.
  • DeepSample lists its samples back to front, as Nuke's panel does, and with accumulate each row is that sample over everything behind it.
  • VectorCornerPin's Bake Corners keeps the user keys and sets smooth keys, as Nuke does; the picture is unchanged.
  • A Projection saved to a .nk now writes its pad for paint as expressions of its own controls, so changing the pad in Nuke resizes everything inside. Before, only the pad menu changed there.
  • In a comp's Python, nuke.createNode wires two selected nodes into a Merge (the first into A, the second into B) and places the new node where Nuke would.

Kento Alpha 0.9.38, build 2998

New

  • VectorRetime's motion blur: shutterSamples and shutterTime now blur the retimed picture, the samples spread evenly over the shutter around each frame and weighted equally, as Nuke renders it.
  • LightKey's alpha bias and despill bias now work, as do the None and Source replace methods with a clip, matching Nuke.

Fixes

  • A movie with a sound track played a frame late inside each run of frames Kento decoded together.
  • A Read set to black before or after its range gave a picture with no channels, so a TimeClip, AppendClip or Keymix past a clip's end had nothing to show. It now gives black with the file's channels.
  • A Bento made from a group with its own controls, such as a transition, lost their values and played as if at the defaults.
  • Matched to Nuke's renders: Copy where A reaches past B, VectorCornerPin between its keys, Stabilize2D's scale factor, TimeClip reversed, TimeOffset's whole frames for negative offsets, CheckerBoard2 on non-square pixels, HSVTool on pixels outside 0 to 1, and AddMix outside A.
